priorStories.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 9,000 cases
priorStories.body:
Congo’s Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths, including 88 new cases in its latest update.

The outbreak has reached 65 health zones across seven provinces. Officials said community transmission was continuing and that many infections remained undetected.

priorStories.headline: Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer
priorStories.body:
Surgery confirmed that Pope Leo XIV has lung adenocarcinoma. Doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung, and the Vatican said the operation was successful.

Decisions about chemotherapy or other treatment will follow additional testing, including an examination of whether the cancer reached his lymph nodes.

priorStories.headline: Drones strike two commercial ships near Bulgaria
priorStories.body:
Drones struck two commercial ships in the Black Sea near Bulgaria, sinking the Guinea-Bissau-flagged Dignity. Five sailors were rescued, while 11 remained missing.

All 15 crew members escaped the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3; five were treated for minor injuries. Bulgarian authorities had not established responsibility. Ukrainian officials blamed Russia.

priorStories.headline: Cyberattack hits 700 French supermarkets
priorStories.body:
A cyberattack targeting connected refrigeration systems affected about 700 supermarkets in France, according to the country’s finance minister. Some stores suffered food losses and fires.

Officials said the incident did not threaten the national food supply. Prosecutors opened an investigation, and no group had publicly claimed responsibility.

priorStories.headline: Bank of America fined over $1.21 billion
priorStories.body:
The Treasury Department imposed more than $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations.

Treasury said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions on time. Bank of America admitted willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act and said it was addressing the compliance failures.

candidates.summary: About 300,000 teachers, health workers, civil servants and other public employees began Ireland’s first widespread public-sector strike since 2009 after unions and the government failed to agree on terms for pay negotiations. Emergency hospital departments and public transport continued operating, but reduced health, fire and ambulance services caused widespread disruption and thousands of canceled medical procedures.
candidates.title: Irish public-sector workers stage nationwide strike

candidates.summary: A Ukrainian presidential adviser said SpaceX imposed a 100 mph operating limit on a military-grade Starlink service in Ukraine without advance notice, disrupting several combat missions. A source in Ukraine’s 7th Rapid Reaction Corps confirmed service disruptions. SpaceX had not publicly explained the reported Ukraine-specific change in the cited report.
candidates.title: Ukraine reports Starlink service limit disrupted military missions

candidates.summary: Germany’s cabinet approved a revised proposal for a tax on sugary drinks, reducing the planned number of tax brackets from three to two and proposing exemptions for small manufacturers. The measure remains pending before parliament and has not taken effect.
candidates.title: German cabinet revises proposed sugary-drink tax

candidates.summary: The U.S. Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% from a year earlier, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported. Gasoline prices increased 9.1% during the month and accounted for more than half of the overall monthly rise. Core prices excluding food and energy rose 0.3% monthly and 2.6% annually.
candidates.title: U.S. inflation rises to 3.7%

candidates.summary: Maritime security sources reported that the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank near the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by a projectile. A Pakistani navigational warning dated October 14 cautioned mariners about floating containers. The ship's manager had not commented, and the report did not identify who launched the projectile.
candidates.title: Container ship sinks near Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: Netflix is cutting about 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 jobs, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing an email sent to employees by its co-chief executives. Reuters said most reductions would affect product, technology, legal and human-resources teams; Netflix had not responded to its request for comment.
candidates.title: Netflix reportedly cuts about 1,000 jobs

candidates.summary: U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the federal government will halt subsidy payments for 189,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees identified as deceased, improperly enrolled or duplicated in other government health programs. He said the action would prevent $738 million in payments during 2026.
candidates.title: U.S. announces halt to subsidies for 189,000 ACA enrollees

candidates.summary: The World Food Programme said intensified fighting had placed about 800,000 people in Yemen beyond its reach, including more than 600,000 aid-dependent residents of besieged Taiz. The International Committee of the Red Cross reported unprecedented numbers of weapon-wounded patients at some front-line hospitals, while the United Nations said more than 200,000 people had recently been displaced.
candidates.title: Yemen fighting cuts aid access to 800,000 people

candidates.summary: Maritime officials confirmed that the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride and Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao sank near the Strait of Hormuz. The GFS Pride was struck while transiting the strait on October 13; all 21 crew members were evacuated without reported injuries. The Cape Dao sank weeks after a September 23 projectile strike that killed one crew member. Responsibility for the attacks was not established in the cited report.
candidates.title: Two commercial ships confirmed sunk near Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: Tens of thousands of students protested in Tirana over education costs, university conditions, corruption and employment prospects. Protesters set fire to the Education Ministry and two banks and threw stones at police, who used tear gas and water cannons. Albanian media reported related protests at universities in Elbasan and Shkodra, while the government condemned the violence.
candidates.title: Albanian student protest turns violent in Tirana

candidates.summary: Colombia opened an embassy in Jerusalem, restoring diplomatic representation in Israel under President Abelardo De La Espriella after his predecessor severed relations in 2024. Colombia’s foreign minister described the opening as a step toward rebuilding bilateral ties. Palestinian Vice President Hussein Al Sheikh condemned the move. A Colombian-Israeli free-trade agreement had been reinstated on October 13.
candidates.title: Colombia opens embassy in Jerusalem

candidates.summary: Guyanese opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed and two other men were arrested after gunfire outside the home of a senior police officer involved in Mohamed’s U.S. extradition proceedings. Police alleged that a shot came from their vehicle and said officers found an unlicensed firearm. Mohamed’s office denied possessing the weapon, accused police of planting it and described the incident as an assassination attempt.
candidates.title: Guyanese opposition leader arrested after shooting incident

candidates.summary: A Danish Meteorological Institute modeling study published in Science Advances found no irreversible tipping point for the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation in the model used: the current weakened as temperatures rose and began recovering if warming was reversed. Researchers said full recovery could take centuries, the Greenland ice sheet would remain irreversibly damaged after melting, and the cooling scenario modeled exceeds what current technology could realistically achieve. The single-model findings require further testing.
candidates.title: Study models possible recovery of weakened Atlantic circulation

candidates.summary: The Vatican said Pope Leo XIV’s recovery after lung-cancer surgery was progressing as expected. He had begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, while blood tests and a chest X-ray showed normal postoperative results. The Vatican said he was expected to remain hospitalized for about a week and canceled his public engagements through October 20.
candidates.title: Vatican reports normal recovery after Pope Leo’s surgery

candidates.summary: Ukraine said an unannounced 100 mph limit on its military-grade Starshield satellite service disrupted drone attack and air-defense missions. Elon Musk said Starshield is owned and controlled by the U.S. government and that its speed and usage limits are decided by the U.S. military and ultimately the president. Former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov later said connectivity at speeds up to 100 mph was being restored but called for the limit’s complete removal.
candidates.title: Ukraine reports Starshield limit disrupted military missions

candidates.summary: North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in its eastern waters, according to state media and South Korea’s military. South Korea said one missile was fired from a vertical launch tube and another from a torpedo tube. The launches were North Korea’s first publicly reported underwater missile tests since January 2024; the exact submarine involved was not officially identified.
candidates.title: North Korea tests two submarine-launched cruise missiles

candidates.summary: Costa Rica inaugurated the High-Containment Center Against Organized Crime, a maximum-security prison near San José modeled on El Salvador’s anti-gang facility. President Laura Fernández said the prison was part of a tougher approach to organized crime. It can hold 5,100 inmates, and officials said the first transfers were scheduled for the end of October.
candidates.title: Costa Rica inaugurates maximum-security mega-prison

candidates.summary: The U.S. Government Accountability Office said Customs and Border Protection and Immigration and Customs Enforcement should improve management of their body-camera programs. Its recommendations included controls such as automatic activation to help ensure ICE cameras record required encounters. The Department of Homeland Security accepted six recommendations but rejected automated activation, citing privacy and operational risks.
candidates.title: DHS rejects automatic activation for ICE body cameras

candidates.summary: ITV released undercover footage showing elected Reform UK councillors and party candidates making racist, anti-Muslim, sexist and violent remarks during election campaigns. Reform UK said investigations had begun and that some people had been suspended. Several people shown had already resigned from the party, while others had not responded to ITV’s findings.
candidates.title: ITV investigation records extreme remarks by Reform UK officials

candidates.summary: The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, affecting about 76 million people receiving Social Security or Supplemental Security Income. Retirement benefits will rise by about $75 per month on average. The increase begins with January 2027 Social Security payments, while higher SSI payments begin December 31, 2026.
candidates.title: U.S. Social Security benefits to rise 3.6% in 2027

candidates.summary: A judge ordered 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis detained after police in Palatine, Illinois, charged him with making a terrorist threat and unlawful weapon possession. Police said a search following his October 11 arrest recovered a rifle, loaded magazines, ammunition, body armor and white-supremacist imagery. Investigators alleged that communications and a document attributed to him indicated a possible mass-shooting plan targeting people of South Asian heritage, potentially at a Hindu place of worship. The specific intended location remained unconfirmed.
candidates.title: Illinois suspect detained over alleged mass-shooting plot
